title: Cycler Finder Catalogue
description: Schema v5.4 (task #736, implementing #735's user-approved design proposal): admits the `#714`->`#729` Jupiter-Europa 3:4 exterior resonant N=5 CRNBP (Circular Restricted N-Body Problem, N=5: spacecraft + Jupiter + Europa + Io + Ganymede) quasi-periodic invariant torus -- a bare torus substitute of Kumar et al. 2021's planar Jupiter-Europa 3:4 exterior resonant periodic orbit, continued to the physical Io mass with Ganymede at its physical (non-rate-idealized) synodic rate and Io exactly Laplace-slaved, in the Baresi/Owen/Scheeres Tri-Circular-Problem model class -- with NO computed manifold connection (unlike the v5.3 `torus_homoclinic` object one system over). Three additive, non-breaking changes: (1) `model_assumption` enum widened with `crnbp` (Circular Restricted N-Body Problem, N>=5 -- a base CR3BP forced by TWO OR MORE additional bodies on concentric circular coplanar orbits, core.crnbp.CRNBPSystem; distinct from `ccr4bp`'s single perturber, since the whole point of this row's second novelty axis is the SECOND simultaneous perturber); (2) `orbit_class` enum widened with `quasi_periodic_torus` (chosen over reusing `torus_homoclinic`, which presupposes a computed manifold connection this object doesn't have and would overclaim; over `resonant_po`, whose strictly-periodic-orbit field conventions and epoch-free invariant cannot honestly encode a 2-D torus with irrational rotation number whose real-ephemeris character is window-structured, not reachable-at-any-epoch; and over the v5.2 epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor `quasi_cycler` subclass, which is cr3bp-scoped, has no real-ephemeris window at all, and characterizes rather than discovers) -- a `quasi_periodic_torus` row is REQUIRED `epoch_locked=true` with `n_returns=1` (one forcing period of demonstrated real-ephemeris model-shadowing per recurring narrow window, NOT a connection's departure-and-return opportunity), enforced by the same Python semantic gate as `quasi_cycler`/`precursor_mga`/`mga_tour`/`torus_homoclinic` (tests/data/test_schema_v47_orbit_class.py); (3) ONE additive, optional, nullable nested row property `crnbp_provenance` ({mu, base_pair, perturbers[] (an N-body LIST mirroring core.crnbp.CRNBPSystem.perturbers 1:1, future-proof for N=6+), resonance_lock, torus{}, real_ephemeris_evidence{} (torus-point-RESOLVED, per `#729`'s own 2-D narrow/collapse dichotomy finding), method}) -- a NEW block, not an extension of `ccr4bp_provenance` (which is scoped to a single named perturber and a computed `connection{}` this object lacks) -- absent/null on every pre-v5.4 row, so it changes NO existing census count. `sequence_canonical` is left null (+ a `data_gaps` `not-applicable` entry, per the `#312`/`#708` rows' own precedent) since there is no alternating named-body flyby sequence to state (neither Io nor Ganymede is ever closely encountered -- both are gravitational perturbers only). See docs/notes/2026-07-27-735-n5-crnbp-torus-catalogue-schema-design.md for the full design reasoning. Schema v5.3 (task #708, implementing #707's user-approved design proposal): admits `#701`'s Uranus Umbriel-Titania CCR4BP torus-homoclinic connection (a spacecraft riding a quasi-periodic invariant torus around a spacecraft:Umbriel 1:2-exterior resonant periodic orbit, departing along the torus's unstable manifold and returning along its stable manifold to machine precision in the idealized model; `#704`/`#705` then showed a comparable near-miss recurs at all 10 tested real-DE440/URA111-ephemeris anchor epochs spanning 2000-2083). This object is structurally unlike every existing row: no flyby of either moon (both stay dynamically irrelevant, encountered only as gravitational forcing terms), and not a single strictly-periodic orbit either (a 2-D invariant torus plus a two-segment manifold connection, not one continuously-propagated loop). Three additive, non-breaking changes: (1) `model_assumption` enum widened with `ccr4bp` (Concentric Circular Restricted 4-Body Problem -- a base 3-body restricted system forced by a THIRD moon on its own circular orbit, structurally distinct from `bicircular`'s Sun-perturbation term); (2) `orbit_class` enum widened with `torus_homoclinic` (chosen over reusing `quasi_cycler`, which presupposes a real multi-body encounter sequence this object doesn't have, and over `resonant_po`, whose defining 'no demonstrated transport utility' property is the opposite of this row's whole point) -- a `torus_homoclinic` row is REQUIRED `epoch_locked=true` with `n_returns=1` (one departure-and-return opportunity per recurring synodic window, real-epoch-anchored evidence -- NOT the `#684` epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor carve-out, which is for objects with no real-ephemeris window at all), enforced by the same Python semantic gate as `quasi_cycler`/`precursor_mga`/`mga_tour` (tests/data/test_schema_v47_orbit_class.py); (3) ONE additive, optional, nullable nested row property `ccr4bp_provenance` ({mu, mu_gan, a_gan, omega_gan, base_resonance, torus_period_tu, torus_rho_strob, torus_closure_residual, connection{}, real_ephemeris_evidence{}, method}), mirroring the `bcr4bp_provenance`/`corridor_measurement` blocks' own additive style exactly -- absent/null on every pre-v5.3 row, so it changes NO existing census count. `sequence_canonical` is left null (+ a `data_gaps` `not-applicable` entry, per the `#312` row's own precedent for genuinely inapplicable fields) since there is no alternating named-body flyby sequence to state. `validity_window`'s `synodic_duty_cycle_pct`/`synodic_boundary_period_days` sub-fields are deliberately NOT populated on this row (only 10 discrete anchor epochs were tested, each with its own dense single-cycle synodic-phase scan -- NOT the continuous multi-year daily scan those fields were built around, per `#569`'s own provenance for them); the within-cycle duty structure is instead carried as a threshold ladder in `ccr4bp_provenance.real_ephemeris_evidence`, a continuous correction-budget concept rather than `#312`'s binary hard-physical-wall criterion. See docs/notes/2026-07-24-707-ccr4bp-catalogue-schema-design.md for the full design reasoning. Schema v5.2 (task #684): resolves a genuine conflict surfaced while writing back #682's cycler-corridor census. #682 measures the quasi-periodic (KAM) torus corridor around already-catalogued, linearly-stable CR3BP periodic orbits (a pure, epoch-free rotating-frame computation — no real ephemeris, no calendar launch window; the torus winds quasi-periodically FOREVER once it exists, per KAM theory). The user decided these become new quasi_cycler rows (one per measured corridor, since corridor size varies 2-3 orders of magnitude within a family and a single-number rollup onto the parent row would lose that structure) — but the v4.7 quasi_cycler invariant (epoch_locked=true + finite n_returns, designed for real-ephemeris 'cyclers of opportunity' like the #569 Uranian moon-pair rows) would force EITHER fabricating a calendar validity_window and a finite return count for an object that has neither, OR reusing resonant_po (rejected: its 'no demonstrated transport utility' semantics conflate awkwardly with the fact that the corridor's PARENT orbits, e.g. the Braik-Ross C21/C32 members, are themselves published transport cyclers). This rev adds a narrowly-scoped, additive exception: a quasi_cycler row MAY be epoch_locked=false / n_returns='infinite' specifically when model_assumption='cr3bp' AND validity_window is null/absent (no real-ephemeris window) — the epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor subclass. Every other quasi_cycler row (the 6 existing #312/#569 Uranian moon-pair rows, all real-ephemeris SPICE-validated with a genuine calendar validity_window) is COMPLETELY UNCHANGED and still hard-required to be epoch_locked=true with a finite n_returns — this is a conditional carve-out, not a weakening of the general rule. Enforced by tests/data/test_schema_v47_orbit_class.py::test_non_cycler_rows_are_epoch_locked_with_finite_returns (the JSON Schema itself cannot express this conditional cross-field rule; it is Python-side, alongside the rest of the orbit_class invariant, which — despite being described in the v4.7 entry below as living in 'the Python semantic gate' — has always lived only in that pytest ratchet, not in src/cyclerfinder/data/validate.py). This rev also adds ONE additive, optional, nullable nested row property, corridor_measurement ({pos_km, vel_ms, amp_nondim, is_lower_bound, closure_residual, method}), mirroring the bcr4bp_provenance block's style (schema v5.0): it records the #682 GMOS-corrector amplitude-ladder KAM-corridor measurement the epoch-free quasi_cycler subclass exists to carry, in particular is_lower_bound — TRUE when the geometric amplitude ladder reached its ceiling with the independent closure residual still passing (the true corridor edge was not found, so the measured pos_km/vel_ms is a LOWER bound on the corridor, not the wall) vs FALSE when a genuine closure-residual wall was found (pos_km/vel_ms IS the edge). No existing field expressed this distinction; data_gaps[] does not fit (it registers known-unknowns, not a measured-but-open-ended bound). Absent/null on every pre-v5.2 row — changes no existing row's validity or census count. Schema v5.1 (task #569 formalization): additively names three synodic-feasibility sub-fields of validity_window — synodic_duty_cycle_pct (number 0-100, feasible fraction of synodic phase from a real epoch-robustness scan), synodic_boundary_period_days (number >0, the measured recurrence period of the feasible/infeasible boundary — NOT always equal to synodic_period_days, e.g. Ariel-Umbriel where it is exactly half), and synodic_period_days (number >0, the moon/body pair's actual synodic period). These were introduced ad hoc by task #569's six Uranian moon-pair quasi_cycler rows as free-form validity_window extras (legal because validity_window already carries additionalProperties:true); this bump only gives them a formal name/type/description on top — no existing row becomes invalid, and no census count changes. All three optional (not required), since most existing rows — including quasi_cycler rows characterized before this pattern existed, such as #312 — carry no epoch-robustness scan. The underlying pattern is general (any epoch-locked multi-body quasi_cycler in any planetary system may need it), not Uranus-specific. Schema v5.0 (task #305): adds ONE additive, optional, nullable nested row property bcr4bp_provenance ({mu_sun, sun_commensurate_n, sun_phase_drift}). Version bumped 4.9 -> 5.0 (not 4.10) because the project's schema-version ratchets compare float(version) (float('4.10') == 4.1 < 4.9, which would silently regress the >= 4.x gates); 5.0 keeps the monotone float ordering. Despite the major-version digit this is a purely additive, backward-compatible change. carrying the BCR4BP (Sun-Earth-Moon bicircular) periodic-orbit provenance that the planar-CR3BP / real-eph fields cannot express, for a future known-reproduction (Andreu / Rosales-Jorba lineage) row admitted via the BCR4BP V0-V5 gauntlet (src/cyclerfinder/data/validation/v{0,1,2,3}_bcr4bp.py). Absent/null on every existing row, so it changes NO census count (verified by the full tests/data tests/search ratchet). Provenance/audit only — not a promotion gate (validation_level carries that). Schema v4.9 (task #453): adds a fifth orbit_class enum value resonant_po — a stable resonant / libration periodic orbit that is reachable at any epoch and repeats indefinitely (so it shares the cycler invariant epoch_locked=false / n_returns='infinite') but has NO demonstrated transport utility (it never encounters the secondary; see Region B #447). Distinct from cycler, whose defining property IS transport between encounters. Added so the catalogue can carry a known-class-member resonant PO (em-cycler-21-3d-spatial-2026, the 3D spatial extension of the planar (2,1) Earth-Moon cycler) without mislabelling it a transport cycler. The resonant_po-is-not-epoch-locked invariant is pinned by tests/data/test_schema_v47_orbit_class.py alongside cycler. Schema v4.8 (task #417): adds two additive optional, nullable row properties encoding the Axis-B real-ephemeris deterministic maintenance-ΔV band taxonomy from docs/notes/2026-06-22-dv-band-definitions.md — dv_band (enum strictly_ballistic/essentially_ballistic/low_maintenance/powered_dsm/low_thrust_sep or null) and its mandatory companion dv_band_source (the published source the band traces to, string or null). Orthogonal to trajectory_regime (Axis-A geometric label): dv_band is the magnitude axis, trajectory_regime the geometric axis. Both default absent/null; a band is assigned ONLY when the row already carries a sourced deterministic maintenance ΔV with a known basis (Russell-Ocampo 2006's <1/<10/<300 m/s-per-7-cycle tiers), never inferred from regime/V∞. The dv_band_source-required-when-dv_band-non-null honesty gate is enforced by the Python semantic gate. Schema v4.7 for data/catalogue.yaml. Task #294: catalogue scope expansion from cyclers-only to a four-class taxonomy (cycler / quasi_cycler / precursor_mga / mga_tour). Adds three additive optional top-level row fields — orbit_class (enum, default cycler for backward compat), epoch_locked (bool, default false), n_returns (integer or the string 'infinite', default 'infinite' for cyclers) — plus three optional epoch-locked fields validity_window {start,end}, launch_epoch, and inserts_into (cross-row pointer used by precursor_mga). The class invariants — cycler MUST be epoch_locked=false / n_returns='infinite'; quasi_cycler / precursor_mga / mga_tour MUST be epoch_locked=true with a finite integer n_returns; precursor_mga MUST resolve inserts_into to an existing cycler row — are enforced by the Python semantic gate (the JSON Schema cannot express cross-row referential integrity). Existing rows default to orbit_class='cycler' / epoch_locked=false / n_returns='infinite' under a one-time migration (scripts/migrate_catalogue_scope_2026-06-15.py), preserving comments and formatting via ruamel.yaml. Supersedes the cyclers-only scope memory (project_catalogue_scope_cyclers_only -> project_catalogue_scope_expanded_2026-06-15). Builds on v4.6, which hardens the previously-freeform discriminator string fields with controlled-vocabulary enums — model_assumption, trajectory_regime, sense, and data_gaps[].kind — each enum being the exact superset of live values plus obviously-intended members. Discovered during #184: model_assumption='bicircular' and data_gaps[].kind='not-applicable' were accepted with zero validation, so a typo (cr3pb, unkown) would pass silently and corrupt the catalogue. Builds on v4.5, which adds the additive optional top-level validation_level enum (V0-V5, the spec §14 gauntlet level; spec §16.7.12), back-filled mechanically by scripts/backfill_validation_level.py from recorded test evidence and guarded against over-claim by validate_validation_level. Builds on v4.4: the per-field provenance tag set orbit_source/vinf_source/orbit_fidelity/vinf_fidelity and the optional declared validation_tier (spec §16.7.11, Forge phase 0 task 3), back-filled mechanically from each row's existing source metadata. source keys are constrained to the SOURCE_REGISTRY enum and fidelity tiers to the Fidelity enum; the declared-tier-must-match-classify_validation rule is enforced by the Python semantic gate. Builds on v4.3 (supersedes/superseded_by, spec §16.7.10), v4.2 (segments[].center, segments[].tof_days_bounds, source_ephemeris, spec §16.7.9), v4.1 (free_return_arcs[] arc-type descriptors, spec §16.7.7) and v4. Permissive on legacy v1-v3 fields (additionalProperties: true throughout); enforces the v4 structural invariants: cycler_class enum, orbit_elements frame/center enums, period.basis item shape, and the conditional physical-invariant gate (multi-arc/non-keplerian must not have top-level a/e). Referential integrity of supersedes/superseded_by (targets must resolve to existing ids, no self-reference) is enforced by the Python semantic gate.

id.description: Stable human-readable slug for this cycler entry.

model_assumption.description: Schema v4.6 (task #194): controlled vocabulary for the dynamical model the row's published numbers were stated under. Enum is the exact superset of live values (circular-coplanar, analytic-ephemeris, cr3bp, bicircular) plus circular-inclined (the M-3D fidelity tier, present in the orbit_fidelity/vinf_fidelity enums) for forward consistency. Constrained because a typo (e.g. 'cr3pb', 'bicirular') would silently corrupt the fidelity derivation. Schema v5.3 (task #707/#708) additively widens the enum with ccr4bp (Concentric Circular Restricted 4-Body Problem -- a base 3-body restricted system, e.g. Uranus-Umbriel, forced by a THIRD moon on its own circular orbit, e.g. Titania -- structurally distinct from bicircular's Sun-perturbation term; using cr3bp for a CCR4BP row would misstate the model, since the whole point of a CCR4BP result is the third-moon forcing term cr3bp lacks). Schema v5.4 (task #735/#736) additively widens the enum with crnbp (Circular Restricted N-Body Problem, N>=5 -- a base CR3BP forced by TWO OR MORE additional bodies on concentric circular coplanar orbits, e.g. Jupiter-Europa forced by BOTH Io and Ganymede; core.crnbp.CRNBPSystem. N is not encoded in the enum value -- it is 2 + 1 + len(crnbp_provenance.perturbers). Distinct from ccr4bp: using ccr4bp for a crnbp row would misstate the model, since the whole point of this row's second novelty axis is the SECOND simultaneous perturber). Reused unmodified for every existing row.

trajectory_regime.description: Schema v4.6 (task #194): controlled vocabulary for the propulsion regime of the trajectory. Enum is the live superset (ballistic, powered) plus low-thrust, the obviously-intended third member of the standard regime trichotomy. Constrained because a typo would pass silently.

sense.description: Schema v4.6 (task #194): controlled vocabulary for the direction sense of the leg. Enum is the exact live superset (outbound, inbound, n/a). Constrained because a typo would pass silently.

data_gaps.description: Schema v4.6 (task #194): the kind discriminator is now a controlled vocabulary. Permissive (additionalProperties: true) on all other gap fields; only kind is constrained.

kind.description: Schema v4.6 (task #194): controlled vocabulary for the gap discriminator. Enum is the exact live superset (unknown, derive, uncertain, not-applicable, unverified-provenance, resolved, conflict, anomaly). Constrained because a typo (e.g. 'unkown', 'not-aplicable') would pass silently and corrupt the review queue, the original #184 failure mode.

source_ephemeris.description: Schema v4.2 (spec §16.7.9): the ephemeris model the source paper states its published numbers were computed against (e.g. 'DE405', 'DE430', 'STOUR ephemeris'). Null/absent when the source does not state one. Non-empty when present (enforced by the Python semantic gate, since JSON Schema minLength cannot apply to the null branch).

orbit_source.description: Schema v4.4 (spec §16.7.11): provenance key (SOURCE_REGISTRY) for the row's orbit-element block (a/e/perihelion/aphelion). Back-filled mechanically from the row's existing source metadata. Absent/null = unknown provenance (untagged); a row left untagged classifies as UNVALIDATED.

vinf_source.description: Schema v4.4 (spec §16.7.11): provenance key (SOURCE_REGISTRY) for the row's vinf_kms_at_encounters multiset. When orbit_source and vinf_source are two DIFFERENT independent citations at the same fidelity, the row is CROSS_VALIDATED. Absent/null = unknown provenance (untagged).

orbit_fidelity.description: Schema v4.4 (spec §16.7.11): model-fidelity tier (Fidelity) the orbit-element block is stated at. Derived from model_assumption. A value at one tier must never be cross-validated against a value at another (the S1L1 cross-fidelity bug class). M-3D additively widened the enum with circular-inclined (real i/Ω, mean sma, eccentricity ignored) between circular-coplanar and analytic-ephemeris.

vinf_fidelity.description: Schema v4.4 (spec §16.7.11): model-fidelity tier (Fidelity) the vinf multiset is stated at. Derived from model_assumption. M-3D additively widened the enum with circular-inclined (real i/Ω, mean sma, eccentricity ignored) between circular-coplanar and analytic-ephemeris.

validation_tier.description: Schema v4.4 (spec §16.7.11): OPTIONAL declared validation tier. When present, the Python semantic gate (validate_provenance_tags) requires it to equal the tier classify_validation computes from the row's sources/fidelities — a row cannot over-claim cross_validated. Normally left absent: the tier is a computed classification (Task 4 ratchet), not stored data.

validation_level.description: Schema v4.5 (spec §16.7.12 / §14): the gauntlet validation level — the highest §14 gate the row has MECHANICALLY passed. Back-filled by scripts/backfill_validation_level.py applying §14 to recorded test evidence. The Python semantic gate (validate_validation_level) refuses any row declaring a level above V0 without a recorded mechanical-evidence pointer (the over-claim guard). Absent/null = untagged (treated as the V0 internal-consistency floor by downstream views).

dv_band.description: Schema v4.8 (task #417): Axis-B real-ephemeris deterministic maintenance-ΔV band, per docs/notes/2026-06-22-dv-band-definitions.md. strictly_ballistic = <1 m/s, essentially_ballistic = <10 m/s, low_maintenance = <300 m/s (Russell-Ocampo 2006 JGCD 29(2) census, total deterministic maneuver over a 7-cycle real-ephemeris propagation at the best launch window); powered_dsm = >=300 m/s impulsive (project-convention boundary = top of Russell's net); low_thrust_sep = SEP/continuous-thrust maintenance (regime, not magnitude). ORTHOGONAL to trajectory_regime (the Axis-A geometric label) — never merge or infer one from the other, and never infer a band from V∞ / v_infinity_leveraging_dv_kms (that is establishment, not maintenance). Absent/null = unclassified (the default for the many rows that carry no sourced per-row maintenance ΔV). When non-null, dv_band_source is mandatory (Python semantic gate).

dv_band_source.description: Schema v4.8 (task #417): the published source the dv_band assignment traces to (e.g. 'byrnes-longuski-aldrin-1993', 'mcconaghy-2006', 'liang-2024'). MANDATORY whenever dv_band is non-null — the honesty gate that every band magnitude traces to a sourced ΔV with a known basis (enforced by the Python semantic gate). Null/absent when dv_band is null.

bcr4bp_provenance.description: Schema v5.0 (task #305): ADDITIVE, OPTIONAL, NULLABLE provenance block for a BCR4BP (Sun-Earth-Moon bicircular) periodic-orbit row admitted via the BCR4BP V0-V5 gauntlet (src/cyclerfinder/data/validation/v{0,1,2,3}_bcr4bp.py). Carried ONLY by a future known-reproduction row sourced from the Andreu / Rosales-Jorba lineage; absent/null for every other row (so it changes NO existing census count). Records the BCR4BP-specific quantities that the planar-CR3BP / real-eph row fields cannot express: mu_sun (Sun mass in Earth+Moon=1 units, the model's perturbation strength), sun_commensurate_n (the integer Sun-synodic commensurability number n in omega_sun*T = 2*pi*n — strict BCR4BP periodicity requires an integer n), and sun_phase_drift (|omega_sun*T - 2*pi*n| rad, the residual Sun-phase mismatch; ~0 iff the orbit is Sun-commensurate, large for a quasi-periodic family member). These are echoed from the BCR4BPPeriodicOrbit the gauntlet validated; they are provenance/audit fields, NOT promotion gates (the validation_level field carries the gate). This is a known-reproduction admission (first_published=Andreu), never a novel discovery; a passing family is flagged for human review, never self-admitted.

mu_sun.description: Sun mass in units where Earth+Moon=1 (BCR4BP perturbation strength). The Andreu / Rosales-Jorba 2023 Table 3 value is 328900.5423094043; mu_sun=0 recovers CR3BP exactly. Null/absent if unrecorded.

sun_commensurate_n.description: Sun-synodic commensurability number n in omega_sun*T = 2*pi*n. Strict BCR4BP periodicity requires a positive integer n; n=1 is one lunar-synodic-period revolution. Null/absent if unrecorded.

sun_phase_drift.description: Residual Sun-phase mismatch |omega_sun*T - 2*pi*n| (rad). ~0 (below the gauntlet's labelled ~1e-6 rad convention) iff the orbit is Sun-commensurate (strictly periodic); large (e.g. ~3.55 rad for the #303 L1 Lyapunov family members) for a quasi-periodic family member that has no strict multi-lap period. Null/absent if unrecorded.

corridor_measurement.description: Schema v5.2 (task #684): ADDITIVE, OPTIONAL, NULLABLE measurement block for a #682 cycler-corridor census row — the KAM quasi-periodic torus corridor around an already-catalogued, linearly-stable CR3BP periodic orbit, measured by the GMOS invariant-circle amplitude-ladder corrector (genome.qp_tori.correct_qp_torus). This is a CHARACTERIZATION of an already-known orbit's surrounding neighborhood, NOT a novel discovery (KAM theory guarantees some such torus family exists around any linearly-stable periodic orbit; the open question #682 answers is purely how BIG). Carried only by the epoch-free CR3BP quasi_cycler subclass rows this rev's orbit_class exception admits; absent/null for every other row (changes NO existing census count). Records the quantities the legacy orbit_elements/invariants blocks cannot express: pos_km/vel_ms (the corridor's transverse tube half-width in position/velocity), amp_nondim (the GMOS amplitude-ladder rung the measurement is pinned at), is_lower_bound (see below), closure_residual (the independent, non-circular short-time nonlinear-flow closure check the ladder rung passed), and method (the corrector identity, for provenance).

pos_km.description: Corridor transverse tube half-width in position, km — max excursion of the GMOS invariant circle from its centroid at the measured amplitude rung. Null/absent if unrecorded.

vel_ms.description: Corridor transverse tube half-width in velocity, m/s — companion to pos_km at the same amplitude rung. Null/absent if unrecorded.

amp_nondim.description: The GMOS eigenvector-displacement amplitude (nondimensional CR3BP units) this measurement is pinned at — the largest rung of the geometric amplitude ladder (data/found/682_cycler_corridor_census: 3e-4, 1e-3, 5e-3, 2e-2, 6e-2) whose torus keeps the independent closure residual below the closure gate. Null/absent if unrecorded.

is_lower_bound.description: TRUE when the amplitude ladder reached its TOP rung with closure still passing — the true corridor edge (wall) was NOT found, so pos_km/vel_ms/amp_nondim are a LOWER bound on the actual corridor, not the wall itself. FALSE when a genuine closure-residual wall was found strictly inside the ladder (the Newton corrector blew up, or the independent closure residual crossed the gate, at the NEXT rung up) — pos_km/vel_ms/amp_nondim then ARE the measured corridor edge. Null/absent if unrecorded. This is the field #684 identified as a genuine pre-v5.2 schema gap: no existing field (data_gaps[] registers known-unknowns, not a measured-but-open-ended bound) could express a genuine KAM wall vs. an amplitude-ladder ceiling.

closure_residual.description: The independent, non-circular short-time nonlinear-CR3BP-flow closure residual (nondimensional) the GMOS torus achieved at the measured amplitude rung — the honest validity gate (#682's CLOSURE_GATE = 1.0e-4 nondim, ~38.44 km equivalent). Null/absent if unrecorded.

method.description: Corrector identity / provenance tag for this measurement, e.g. 'gmos-amplitude-ladder' (genome.qp_tori.correct_qp_torus, the Olikara-Scheeres GMOS benchmark corrector — #682's own positive control: tests/search/test_variational_qp_torus.py::test_l2_positive_control_reproduces_gmos_torus). Null/absent if unrecorded.

ccr4bp_provenance.description: Schema v5.3 (task #707/#708): ADDITIVE, OPTIONAL, NULLABLE provenance block for a CCR4BP (Concentric Circular Restricted 4-Body Problem) torus-homoclinic-connection row (orbit_class='torus_homoclinic'), admitted per the #689-#708 pipeline (core.ccr4bp / core.ccr4bp_umbriel_titania / search.variational_ccr4bp_torus / search.ccr4bp_manifold_globalize / search.ccr4bp_heteroclinic_search / search.ccr4bp_real_ephemeris_consistency). Mirrors bcr4bp_provenance's own additive pattern exactly. Absent/null for every other row (changes NO existing census count). Carries the CCR4BP system parameters, the idealized-model connection's own geometric identity, and the real-ephemeris recurrence evidence that the planar-CR3BP / real-eph row fields cannot express. Provenance/audit only — not a promotion gate (validation_level carries that).

mu.description: Base moon's CR3BP mass ratio, GM_moon / (GM_primary_system + GM_moon) -- e.g. Umbriel's mass ratio in the Uranus-Umbriel two-body reduction. mu=0 has no special meaning here (unlike bcr4bp's mu_sun=0 CR3BP-exact reduction) since mu is the BASE system's own mass ratio, not the perturbation strength. Null/absent if unrecorded.

mu_gan.description: Perturbing (third) moon's nondimensional mass in the base system's mass unit, GM_perturber / (GM_primary_system + GM_base_moon) -- e.g. Titania's mass ratio in the Uranus-Umbriel mass unit. Field name kept consistent with core.ccr4bp.CCR4BPSystem's own mu_gan attribute (historically named after Ganymede, the perturber in the first-built Jupiter-Europa-Ganymede system) even when the actual perturbing body is not Ganymede -- avoids a translation-layer name mismatch between this provenance block and the code that produced it. mu_gan=0 recovers CR3BP exactly (structural sanity check, per core.ccr4bp's own docstring). Null/absent if unrecorded.

a_gan.description: Perturbing moon's semi-major axis in base-moon-SMA units (e.g. Titania SMA / Umbriel SMA, ~1.640 for Uranus-Umbriel-Titania). Same mu_gan-derived naming convention. Null/absent if unrecorded.

omega_gan.description: Perturbing moon's synodic angular rate in the base system's rotating frame (n_perturber/n_base - 1; negative when the perturber is the slower-moving outer body, per core.ccr4bp.two_body_synodic_rate). Same mu_gan-derived naming convention. Null/absent if unrecorded.

base_resonance.description: Descriptive tag for the base periodic orbit the torus is built around, e.g. 'spacecraft:Umbriel=1:2-exterior' -- echoed into orbit_elements.cr3bp.family as well; kept here too so ccr4bp_provenance is self-contained. Null/absent if unrecorded.

torus_period_tu.description: Base torus's own stroboscopic-map period, nondimensional time units (TU) of the base CR3BP system. Echoed into orbit_elements.cr3bp.period_nd. Null/absent if unrecorded.

torus_rho_strob.description: Stroboscopic-map rotation number (rho) of the invariant torus -- the quasi-periodic winding rate transverse to the base periodic orbit. Null/absent if unrecorded.

torus_closure_residual.description: The GMOS-style (or equivalent) torus corrector's own closure residual at convergence, nondimensional -- the torus construction's own validity gate, analogous to corridor_measurement.closure_residual. Null/absent if unrecorded.

connection.description: The idealized-CCR4BP homoclinic/heteroclinic connection's own geometric identity, as produced by search.ccr4bp_heteroclinic_search.RefinedConnection + GhostGuardReport.

theta2_u.description: Unstable-manifold departure phase (torus's second angle coordinate), radians.

t_u_tu.description: Unstable-branch elapsed flow time, nondimensional TU.

t_u_days.description: Same, converted to days via this row's own physical time unit.

t_s_tu.description: Stable-branch elapsed flow time, nondimensional TU.

idealized_pos_gap_km.description: Position mismatch at the refined connection's local optimum, idealized CCR4BP model, km.

idealized_vel_gap_km_s.description: Velocity mismatch at the refined connection's local optimum, idealized CCR4BP model, km/s.

off_torus_km.description: Ghost-guard off-torus sanity distance -- how far the departure state is from the unperturbed torus at the same elapsed time (rules out a trivial near-departure pseudo-match), km.

quasi_jacobi_gap.description: Base-CR3BP Jacobi-constant gap between the two connection endpoints (search.ccr4bp_heteroclinic_search.quasi_jacobi_gap) -- an APPROXIMATE physical-plausibility check, not an exact conserved quantity (the CCR4BP has none). Reported, not gated.

integrator_delta_km.description: Ghost-guard independent-integrator (Radau vs. DOP853) consistency check: the km difference between the two integrators' position-gap estimate for the same connection. Small = genuine physics, not a chaos-amplified numerical artifact.

residual_norm.description: The 4-unknown least-squares refinement's own converged residual norm (nondimensional).

real_ephemeris_evidence.description: Real-ephemeris consistency + epoch-recurrence evidence for this connection (the #704/#705 findings). Distinct in kind from validity_window's synodic_duty_cycle_pct trio (v5.1) -- see the #707 design note Q4 for why this connection's evidence is a continuous correction-magnitude ladder at sparse discrete epochs, not a dense binary-feasibility scan.

force_model.description: Real-ephemeris force-model identity/kernel used for reconstruction, e.g. 'DE440 + URA111, n-body'.

comparable_pos_gap_threshold_km.description: Pre-declared 'comparable to the reference near-miss' position-gap gate used to judge epoch recurrence (e.g. 10x the reference epoch's own best point).

tested_epochs.description: One entry per independently-tested real-ephemeris anchor epoch.

base_epoch_utc.description: ISO-8601 anchor epoch this synodic-phase scan was centered on.

local_minimum_epoch_utc.description: ISO-8601 epoch of the best (locally-minimized) near-miss point found within this anchor's synodic-phase scan.

closest_approach_km.description: Closest approach distance to each dynamically-relevant body during this local-minimum trajectory, km -- the collision-course sanity check (both moons' physical radii are far smaller than every observed value here).

comparable_to_reference.description: Whether this epoch's local minimum passed the comparable_pos_gap_threshold_km/comparable_vel_gap_threshold_km_s gate.

fraction_epochs_comparable.description: n_epochs_comparable / n_epochs_tested -- the epoch-recurrence verdict fraction.

synodic_duty_cycle_bands_pct.description: Fraction of ONE synodic cycle (at a representative anchor epoch) for which the position mismatch is below each of several thresholds -- a continuous correction-budget ladder, NOT a single binary feasible/infeasible fraction (see validity_window.synodic_duty_cycle_pct's own docstring for the contrast). Keys are threshold labels (e.g. 'below_500km'), values are {fraction_of_period, n_distinct_windows}.

resolution_caveat.description: Honest statement of the evidence's own resolution limits (e.g. epoch spacing, points-per-cycle) -- mandatory whenever tested_epochs is non-null, mirroring dv_band_source's non-null-requires-source pattern.

method.description: Corrector/search-pipeline identity/provenance tag, e.g. 'ccr4bp-manifold-globalize+heteroclinic-search+ghost-guard' (search.variational_ccr4bp_torus + search.ccr4bp_manifold_globalize + search.ccr4bp_heteroclinic_search). Null/absent if unrecorded.

crnbp_provenance.description: Schema v5.4 (task #735/#736): ADDITIVE, OPTIONAL, NULLABLE provenance block for a CRNBP (Circular Restricted N-Body Problem, N>=5) row (orbit_class='quasi_periodic_torus'), admitted per the #714-#729 pipeline (core.crnbp / search.variational_crnbp_torus / search.crnbp_real_ephemeris_consistency). Mirrors ccr4bp_provenance's additive pattern but generalizes the perturber parameters to a LIST (matching core.crnbp.CRNBPSystem.perturbers exactly), so N=6+ needs no schema change. Absent/null for every other row (changes NO existing census count). Provenance/audit only -- not a promotion gate.

mu.description: BASE system's CR3BP mass ratio, GM_secondary / (GM_primary_system + GM_secondary) -- e.g. Europa's ratio in the Jupiter-Europa reduction (core.crnbp.CRNBPSystem.mu).

base_pair.description: Human-readable base-system tag, e.g. 'Jupiter-Europa'. The rotating frame, DU, and TU are this pair's.

perturbers.description: One entry per extra perturbing body, IN THE SAME ORDER as core.crnbp.CRNBPSystem.perturbers in the producing run (order is load-bearing for reproduction). Each mirrors core.crnbp.CRNBPPerturber field-for-field, plus provenance strings.

mu.description: Nondimensional mass GM_j/(GM_primary_sys+GM_secondary), base-system mass unit (CRNBPPerturber.mu).

omega.description: Synodic angular rate in the base rotating frame, n_j/n2 - 1 (CRNBPPerturber.omega).

rate_provenance.description: How omega was set: registry-derived physical rate, resonance-projected (e.g. 'laplace-projected: omega_io = -2*omega_gan exactly'), or idealized -- the honesty axis #724's rate-model novelty claim rests on.

resonance_lock.description: The multi-perturber commensurability making the forcing single-clock periodic, with its phase constraint -- e.g. 'Galilean Laplace lock: omega_io = -2*omega_gan exact (observed-period ratio -2.000000001); phi_L = theta_io0 + 2*theta_gan0 = pi (physical libration center, Sinclair 1975)'. Null if the perturbers are independently periodic (no such row yet).

torus.description: The quasi-periodic torus's own identity and convergence evidence (search.variational_crnbp_torus.CRNBPTorusVariationalResult). The analogue of ccr4bp_provenance's torus_* scalars plus the seed/continuation lineage that IS this object's positive control (#714: no literature-grade N=5 dynamical control exists; the control is continuation from the validated N=4 limit).

base_resonance.description: Base periodic orbit tag, e.g. 'spacecraft:Europa=3:4-exterior (Kumar et al. 2021 class)'. Echoed into orbit_elements.cr3bp.family.

period_tu.description: Stroboscopic forcing period (theta1 clock, = period_multiple Ganymede-synodic cycles), nondim TU. Echoed into orbit_elements.cr3bp.period_nd.

rho_strob.description: Stroboscopic-map rotation number, matching ccr4bp_provenance.torus_rho_strob's convention.

residual_rms.description: On-grid pseudospectral collocation residual RMS at convergence.

closure_residual.description: Independent nonlinear flow-closure residual (search.variational_crnbp_torus._independent_closure: full coupling-term-included crnbp_eom DOP853 flow vs the Fourier surface -- methodologically independent of the algebraic solve). MANDATORY to quote alongside residual_rms per #724 ('off-grid invariance ~2.1e-3 alongside the on-grid 1.23e-4'), since it is the truncation-floor-limited number.

seed_lineage.description: Full continuation chain from the validated anchor, e.g. 'Kumar-2021 JE 3:4 exterior resonant PO (CR3BP) -> #690 CCR4BP torus (n1=2,n2=20) -> mu_io=0 CRNBP seed -> 8-step mu_Io continuation to physical 4.7043400305e-05'.

real_ephemeris_evidence.description: Real-ephemeris MODEL-SHADOWING evidence (the #726/#729 findings): idealized-CRNBP forward flow of a chosen torus point over one forcing period vs real-SPICE propagation of the same departure state -- a position/velocity mismatch at the comparison time, NOT a connection-quality metric (no manifold pair exists for this object class). Torus-point-RESOLVED: #729's narrow/collapse dichotomy is torus-point-dependent but epoch-stable, and that 2-D structure is the evidence.

check_type.description: e.g. 'model-shadowing over one Ganymede-synodic forcing period (search.crnbp_real_ephemeris_consistency.check_torus_survives_real_ephemeris)'.

forcing_period_days.description: The real forcing (Ganymede-synodic) period the check propagates over, days.

narrow_near_miss_threshold_km.description: #729's pre-declared ABSOLUTE narrow-window gate (5000 km) -- unlike ccr4bp_provenance's relative comparable_*_threshold (no reference connection exists here).

positive_control.description: The checker's own validity gate: {pos_gap_km, vel_gap_km_s, note} for a case where model and reality MUST agree (#726: 1.75e-2 km / 1.13e-7 km/s).

generic_collapse_reference.description: The off-window magnitude that makes 'narrow' meaningful: #726's headline naive-epoch gap {pos_gap_km, vel_gap_km_s, epoch_utc, noise_floor_note}.

torus_points.description: One entry per tested torus point (theta1_0, theta2_0) -- the #729 second scan axis.

epoch_stability_note.description: The torus-point-dependent-but-epoch-stable dichotomy statement (#729's key structural finding).

synodic_duty_cycle_bands_pct.description: Identical shape to ccr4bp_provenance's own synodic_duty_cycle_bands_pct -- threshold-label keys -> {fraction_of_period, n_distinct_windows}; measured at ONE representative (torus_point, anchor).

resolution_caveat.description: Mandatory whenever torus_points is non-null (same rule as ccr4bp_provenance).

flyby_altitudes_km.description: Schema v4.9 (task #427, M7): per-interior-flyby minimal-thrust periapsis ALTITUDE (km above the body surface) — the height that delivers the node's required turn ballistically (Jones Eq.2), capped at the body's sourced flyby floor (#426) where the turn over-demands. Sourced where a paper publishes per-flyby altitudes; otherwise computed by the M7 continuous-maintenance chain (flyby_altitudes_source distinguishes). Null/absent for the many rows with no reproduced trajectory (honest — never fabricated). Distinct from a single floor: each node carries its own optimal height.

node_index.description: Index of this flyby encounter within the cycler's node sequence.

body.description: One-letter flyby body code (e.g. 'E', 'M') matching the PLANETS registry.

altitude_km.description: Minimal-thrust periapsis altitude above the body surface, km. At the body floor (#426) when the flyby is bend-binding (then the node carries a maintenance ΔV); higher for gentle flybys that need less turn.

flyby_altitudes_source.description: Schema v4.9 (tasks #427/#428): provenance of flyby_altitudes_km. 'sourced' = published per-flyby altitudes (literature-stated); 'computed-m7' = computed by the M7 continuous-maintenance chain (geometry-determined minimal-thrust heights); 'derived' = SPK/Horizons-extracted per-flyby altitudes (our own reconstruction — high fidelity but not literature-sourced, so not golden-test-eligible). Sourced takes precedence. Null/absent when flyby_altitudes_km is null.

superseded_by.description: Schema v4.3 (spec §16.7.10): ids of catalogue rows that supersede this one (CCSDS NEXT_MESSAGE_ID analogue). Used when a row's premise is invalidated and one or more sibling rows now carry the attested truth. Each item must resolve to an existing row id and must not equal this row's own id; referential integrity is checked by the Python semantic gate. Null/absent for the common (non-superseded) case.

supersedes.description: Schema v4.3 (spec §16.7.10): ids of catalogue rows that this row supersedes (CCSDS PREVIOUS_MESSAGE_ID analogue). The inverse direction of superseded_by; the pair need not be declared symmetrically, but every id listed must resolve to an existing row and must not equal this row's own id (Python semantic gate). Null/absent for the common case.

cycler_class.description: Structural kind of orbit. Default single-ellipse preserves v3 behaviour.

orbit_class.description: Schema v4.7 (task #294, spec/catalogue-scope-expanded-2026-06-15): mission-actionable orbit class. cycler = strictly periodic, NOT epoch_locked, n_returns=infinite, transports between encounters (the original scope; Aldrin, Russell-Ocampo, Braik-Ross). quasi_cycler = closes-up-to-rotation, epoch_locked, 3-15 returns inside a planetary-alignment window (cyclers of opportunity) — EXCEPT the epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor subclass (schema v5.2, task #684: model_assumption='cr3bp' AND validity_window null/absent), which is instead NOT epoch_locked / n_returns=infinite, since a quasi-periodic torus around a linearly-stable CR3BP orbit winds forever with no calendar window to speak of; see corridor_measurement and the top-level v5.2 description entry. precursor_mga = non-repeating MGA chain that inserts a spacecraft INTO a steady-state cycler, epoch_locked, n_returns=1, MUST set inserts_into to an existing cycler row id. mga_tour = non-repeating multi-gravity-assist tour terminating at a destination (Galileo VEEGA, Cassini VVEJGA, Tito 2018 Mars free-return), epoch_locked, n_returns=1. resonant_po (schema v4.9, task #453) = a stable resonant / libration periodic orbit: NOT epoch_locked, n_returns=infinite (shares the cycler reachability/periodicity invariants) but with NO demonstrated transport utility — it never encounters the secondary (Region B #447). Carried for known-class corroboration, not as a usable cycler. torus_homoclinic (schema v5.3, task #707/#708) = a homoclinic connection to a quasi-periodic invariant torus in a CCR4BP (departs the torus's unstable manifold, returns via its stable manifold to the SAME torus) — epoch_locked=true, n_returns=1 (ONE departure-and-return opportunity per recurring real-ephemeris synodic window; a real-epoch-anchored result, unlike the epoch-free quasi_cycler CR3BP-KAM-corridor carve-out above). Distinct from quasi_cycler: no named-body encounter exists at all (neither moon is ever closely approached — see ccr4bp_provenance.real_ephemeris_evidence), and the 'recurrence' is the SAME one-shot opportunity reappearing each synodic cycle, not consecutive flights of an identical multi-leg flyby tour. Distinct from resonant_po: the whole point is a demonstrated transport connection (depart the torus, arrive back via a different route), not the absence of one. quasi_periodic_torus (schema v5.4, task #735/#736) = a bare quasi-periodic invariant torus — a dynamical substitute of a periodic orbit under time-periodic forcing (CCR4BP/CRNBP/QBCP class) — with NO computed manifold connection: epoch_locked=true, n_returns=1 (one forcing period of demonstrated real-ephemeris model-shadowing per recurring narrow window — NOT a torus_homoclinic connection's departure-and-return opportunity, and NOT resonant_po's reachable-at-any-epoch invariant, since the real ephemeris shows GENERIC COLLAPSE off the recurring narrow window). Distinct from torus_homoclinic: its connection{} payload (departs/returns, manifold segments) is populated for that class and has no referent here — no manifold has been globalized and no connection attempted for this object. Distinct from the v5.2 epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor quasi_cycler subclass: that subclass is model_assumption='cr3bp'-scoped, characterizes the corridor around an ALREADY-catalogued stable CR3BP orbit (KAM theory guarantees existence — not a novel discovery), and has no real-ephemeris window at all; a quasi_periodic_torus row's forcing model IS the object's point and its real-ephemeris shadowing evidence, where present, is the row's headline. Distinct from resonant_po: the underlying object is a 2-D torus with irrational rotation number, not a strictly-periodic orbit encodable in orbit_elements.cr3bp's single-IC/single-period/Floquet-stability field conventions. Default cycler preserves v4.6 behaviour: every pre-v4.7 row is a cycler.

epoch_locked.description: Schema v4.7 (task #294): true when the trajectory exists only inside a specific real-ephemeris launch window (the epoch-locked classes), false for strictly periodic orbits reachable at any epoch. Default false preserves v4.6 behaviour. The test_schema_v47_orbit_class ratchet enforces orbit_class in {cycler, resonant_po} => epoch_locked=false / n_returns='infinite' and orbit_class in {quasi_cycler, precursor_mga, mga_tour} => epoch_locked=true with a finite integer n_returns — EXCEPT (schema v5.2, task #684) a quasi_cycler row with model_assumption='cr3bp' and validity_window null/absent, which is the epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor subclass and is instead required to be epoch_locked=false / n_returns='infinite', like cycler/resonant_po. This is a narrow, conditional carve-out; every other quasi_cycler/precursor_mga/mga_tour row is unaffected.

n_returns.description: Schema v4.7 (task #294): number of cycler-style returns the trajectory completes within its validity window. The literal string 'infinite' for strictly periodic cyclers (the v4.6-and-prior default), a positive integer otherwise (1 for precursor_mga / mga_tour, 3-15 for quasi_cycler) — EXCEPT (schema v5.2, task #684) the epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor quasi_cycler subclass (model_assumption='cr3bp', validity_window null/absent), which carries 'infinite' like a cycler (a KAM torus winds quasi-periodically forever; there is no finite return count to state). Default 'infinite' preserves v4.6 behaviour.

validity_window.description: Schema v4.7 (task #294): real-ephemeris window during which the trajectory closes. Required (non-null) for epoch_locked classes; null/absent for cyclers (which have no window — they close at any epoch) AND (schema v5.2, task #684) for the epoch-free CR3BP KAM-corridor quasi_cycler subclass (model_assumption='cr3bp' rows with no real-ephemeris window are exactly the diagnostic condition for that subclass — see orbit_class/epoch_locked/n_returns). Schema v5.1 (task #569 formalization) additively names three synodic-feasibility sub-fields — synodic_duty_cycle_pct, synodic_boundary_period_days, synodic_period_days — that generalize beyond the Uranian moon-pair rows they were introduced for: any epoch-locked multi-body quasi_cycler can be characterized by an epoch-robustness scan yielding a recurring feasible/infeasible duty cycle. All three were already legal under additionalProperties:true; this only gives them a formal name/type/description so future writebacks don't reinvent or hand-copy the convention. All three optional; meaningful only when a real epoch-robustness scan (not a single-epoch pass/fail) has characterized the row.

start.description: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC) for the earliest epoch at which the trajectory closes within tolerance.

end.description: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC) for the latest epoch at which the trajectory closes within tolerance.

synodic_duty_cycle_pct.description: Schema v5.1 (task #569 formalization): percentage of synodic phase for which the candidate is dynamically feasible (V4-strict-passing), measured from a real multi-epoch robustness scan (e.g. daily sampling across one or more synodic cycles) — NOT a single-epoch pass/fail. Feasible fraction = n_PASS / (n_PASS + n_infeasible) over the scanned epochs. Optional; present only when such a scan has been run (e.g. the six #569 Uranian moon-pair quasi_cycler rows, per the #567/#568 epoch-robustness scan + verdict).

synodic_boundary_period_days.description: Schema v5.1 (task #569 formalization): the period (days) at which the feasible/infeasible boundary recurs, measured as the dominant FFT period of the daily feasibility-boundary series from the epoch-robustness scan. For most candidates this equals the full synodic_period_days, but it is NOT reliably derivable from synodic_period_days alone — for the Ariel-Umbriel #569 row the boundary recurs TWICE per synodic cycle (a symmetric geometry specific to that pair), so synodic_boundary_period_days there is exactly HALF of synodic_period_days (3.2 d vs 6.4322 d). Always state both fields independently rather than assuming a fixed ratio. Optional; present only alongside synodic_duty_cycle_pct.

synodic_period_days.description: Schema v5.1 (task #569 formalization): the moon/body pair's actual synodic period in days (the full, undivided value), independent of and not necessarily equal to synodic_boundary_period_days (see that field's description for the Ariel-Umbriel halving counterexample). Optional; present only alongside synodic_duty_cycle_pct.

launch_epoch.description: Schema v4.7 (task #294): ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC) for the published / reproduced launch epoch of an mga_tour or precursor_mga row. Null/absent for cyclers and for quasi_cyclers (which have a validity_window but not a single launch_epoch).

inserts_into.description: Schema v4.7 (task #294): catalogue row id of the steady-state cycler this precursor_mga inserts a spacecraft into. REQUIRED (non-null) when orbit_class='precursor_mga' (enforced by the Python semantic gate, which also verifies the target id resolves to an existing cycler row). Null/absent otherwise.

free_return_arcs.description: Schema v4.1 (spec §16.7.7): Russell's Earth-to-Earth free-return arc decomposition. Distinct from trajectory.segments (encounter legs). Each item is one Earth-Earth arc in Russell's notation. Null when no descriptor is available (data gap, not error). Only meaningful for multi-arc cyclers (no-op on single-ellipse / non-keplerian).

arc_type.description: Russell free-return arc type. g/G=generic, h/H=half-rev, f/F=full-rev.

resonance.description: Resonance ratio string (e.g. '3:2', '2:1', '1:1') for full-rev arcs. Always null for generic and half-rev.

tof_years.description: Time of flight in years for this Earth-Earth arc. Per Russell p.127: 'the first number in the parenthesis is the time of flight in years'. Null for full-rev arcs where TOF is determined by the M:N resonance condition, not listed explicitly.

raw_descriptor.description: Verbatim Russell descriptor token, e.g. 'g(1.4612,526.02,Ll)' or 'F(3:2,82.487,180.000)'. Preserved exactly so nothing is lost to interpretation. The arc_type/resonance fields are derived from this string.

a_au.description: Semi-major axis in AU. Null for multi-arc and non-keplerian.

e.description: Eccentricity. Null for multi-arc and non-keplerian.

cr3bp.description: CR3BP identity tuple for non-keplerian orbits.

invariants.description: Cycle-level identity descriptors for multi-arc orbits.

segments.description: OCM TRAJ-model encounter legs. Permissive (additionalProperties: true) on legacy keys; v4.2 only constrains the two additive optional keys center and tof_days_bounds.

center.description: Schema v4.2 (spec §16.7.9): body the segment's conic/arc is centred on. Absent => 'Sun' (heliocentric, the status quo). Free string (consistent with orbit_elements.center); no enum, to allow planet-centric (moon-tour) cycler segments (issue #76).

tof_days_bounds.description: Schema v4.2 (spec §16.7.9): published time-of-flight range [min, max] in days, for sources stating a range rather than a point. Both > 0 and min <= max (order enforced by the Python semantic gate). NOT required to contain tof_days when present — different model framings of the same leg may both be sourced (e.g. Aldrin outbound tof_days=146 circular-coplanar vs Rogers et al. 2012 STOUR range 161-172 d).
